description: No patch-automerge: PeerTube runs its database migrations unattended on startup, and its patch releases do carry them - of the 15 patch spans examined, v8.1.2 -> v8.1.3 added a migration re-encoding every actor's federation key and v8.1.7 -> v8.1.8 one invalidating all OAuth tokens. Version bumps stay human-reviewed pull requests here.

The extractVersion rule below is what makes those pull requests appear at all: the 6.x/7.x line is published only as Debian-flavoured tags (`v7.3.0-bookworm`, never a plain `v7.3.0`), which strict semver could not read, so this role saw no update for a year. The rule is tied to `peertube_distro_variant`, and a move to 8.x - whose plain tags replace the deprecated Debian suffix - has to change both.

packageRules.description: Read versions out of the `-bookworm` tags that peertube_container_image_tag composes, ignoring the other Debian flavours and the floating `production`/`develop` tags
